apiSketch.convention: copies src/surfaces.tsx: components own no styling and declare no token, colour, radius, duration or type step; every prop is content or a named semantic state; className and style are removed at src/base.ts.

components: Cite - the local-ordinance form. {children} {marker}. children is the local short form; marker is the word in the em slot (the specimen's 'local').
ModelCite - the licensed form. corpus and section both required. Renders .
cite.inversionTrapAddressed: TRAP 1, the licensed form must have NO body slot. ModelCite is a SEPARATE component, not a boolean on Cite, and its prop type is Omit<AnchorBase, "children"> so children is not in the props type at all. Passing JSX children is a compile error, not a review comment. Two instruments hold it: a law test asserting the Omit is present in source, and a consumer MUST_NOT_COMPILE case watching tsc reject a ModelCite carrying body text on the offending line. The absence is the enforcement mechanism, so it is enforced by the type rather than documented.

components: AtomChip - the openable form. . record required. unservable adds .dead and stays a button, because an unservable record still opens and degrades to local BRIEF plus full record unavailable.
UnverifiedSource - the .web form. {children}. A span, not a button; no aria-expanded, no record slot, no unservable arm.
atomchip.inversionTrapAddressed: different ELEMENTS, not a prop on one element, per ruling G2 and the platform IA markup contract. A `web` boolean on AtomChip would have produced a button with aria-expanded for a source that cannot be opened, and would have let an unverified source inherit the openable affordance the reserved accent is a promise about. .atomchip.web already drops --sc-atom for neutral ink in CSS; the split keeps the same separation at the API.

components: MatrixGroup - the corpus header. corpus required (the FULL canonical title; an abbreviation alone is prohibited), licence required (the .lic badge), optional children for a trailing section count through the existing global .grow.

MatrixRow -
{children}
. applicability REQUIRED with no default; section required; children is the status pill.
mx.inversionTrapAddressed: TRAP 2, applicability is inverted. applicability has NO DEFAULT VALUE. The kit's precedent for a defaulted prop is Pill, where omission is the QUIETEST form because that is what law 3 wants; here the quietest form is pass, so copying that pattern would make an unreviewed row render as reviewed by omission. This follows the EnvBadge precedent instead, where there is deliberately no default so a demo can never render as live by omission. Four instruments: a law test asserting the source carries no applicability default, a law test asserting the four values map to the four state classes and that the pass arm adds no carrier beyond mx-pass, a consumer MUST_NOT_COMPILE case watching tsc reject a MatrixRow with no applicability, and a prove:gates case that injects a pass default and watches the law test fire.

components:
BasisLine -
. sources and read REQUIRED. confidence optional and a single object { state, level, of } so a level can never be given without its state. When present it renders Confidence ... {state}, which is where the f class comes from.

Finding -
{children}
{actions}
. identifier, title and basis all required; critical adds .crit; basis is the BasisLine's own props object, so Finding CONSTRUCTS the basis line rather than accepting one.
finding.inversionTrapAddressed: TRAP 3, a confidence value cannot render without what earns it. There is NO exported Meter component and no standalone confidence prop anywhere: the meter exists only inside BasisLine, which requires sources and read. Finding takes basis as BasisLine's props and renders the BasisLine itself, so a finding with a confidence but no basis line is not expressible at either layer. A ReactNode slot was considered and rejected: JSX.Element is ReactElement<any> in React 19, so a basis: ReactElement<BasisLineProps> type would have been vacuous and any element would have satisfied it. Held by a law test that renders a Finding with a confidence and asserts the sources and read text are both in the output, a consumer MUST_NOT_COMPILE case for a BasisLine carrying confidence with no sources or read, and a prove:gates case that removes the read slot and watches the law test fire.
